channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description: Ferguson is set to handle No. 2 pass-catcher duties with WR Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined this week. The young tight end posted a 6/54/1 receiving line in Week 2 and can be viewed as a TE1 in this matchup.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cardinals qB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the 49ers.
item.description: Brissett practiced fully all week, despite the hip injury. Brissett is not quite hitting the peaks he produced last year and is too tough to trust in 12-team leagues. Consider him a QB2 against the 49ers this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description: The Cardinals lost their top perimeter CB Will Johnson (neck) to injured reserve this week. Fellow perimeter CB Max Melton (toe) is questionable to play. Williams suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture last year, and returns this week to man the slot.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (stinger/foot) is doubtful for Week 3 against the Chiefs.
item.description: Wright was unable to practice on Friday. He is very unlikely to play, although his absence may only be felt in the return game. Dolphins RBOllie Gordonwill serve as the top backup.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) is questionable to play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description: Evans did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was in uniform and warming up during the open portion of Friday’s practice. When asked whether Evans was limited or full, he declined to say. If Evans was full, we have almost no concerns about his ability to play this week, though he likely would have been removed from the injury report if that were the case. Evans must be treated as truly questionable to play, so make a backup plan, but he is the type of player who does not necessarily need to practice fully before practicing. If active, he is a WR2.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bears K Cairo Santos (right hip) did not practice on Friday.
item.description: Santos has tumbled from the potential beneficiary of a potent offense to a droppable player in 12-team leagues. He is also on the wrong side of questionable.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description: Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Commanders S Nick Cross (illness) won’t play in Washington’s Week 3 game against the Seahawks.
item.description: He didn’t practice all week after spending Sunday night in a Dallas hospital following an “internal injury” he suffered against the Cowboys. Sounds ominous. We’d be unsurprised if Cross were placed on injured reserve on Saturday.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Seahawks ruled out S Julian Love (calf) for Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description: The Seahawks also ruled out S Ty Okada (hamstring) for this week’s game. Okada has not yet played in 2026. Love injured his calf in practice this week. The Seahawks’ D/ST remains a worthwhile play against the Commanders, thanks to the defense’s overall talent and coach Mike Macdonald’s top-tier scheming. Losing the two safeties will simply complicate Macdonald’s preferred three-safety looks.-Nic Bodiford
